thread:
andrew-vendor: Quick heads-up — FRA depot flagged a quarantine on a 20-unit H100 batch. During burn-in we saw a NIC firmware mismatch causing intermittent link flaps and PXE failures. Holding units pending next steps.

devon: ugh. do we have the firmware versions and failing logs? we need to know if this is flashable at depot or full RMA.

andrew-vendor: Firmware on the lot = 1.2.4 (board), network fw = 0.9.1. Our burn-in shows repeated link down/up and `kernel: mlx5` errors. Depot can reflash NIC firmware to 0.9.4 on-site (48–72h) or we can process RMA/exchange for factory-refurbished units (air expedite ~72h but with customs paperwork).

raj: reproducing the symptom in staging — nodes drop during kernel init when NIC firmware mismatch occurs. snippet from node-console:```
[  12.345678] mlx5_core 0000:3b:00.0: NIC firmware mismatch: expected 0.9.4, found 0.9.1
[  12.345682] mlx5_core 0000:3b:00.0: link state changed to DOWN
[  12.345690] kubelet: liveness probe failed for pod/gpu-smoke-test
```

maya: If depot reflashes, do we need a re-qualification burn before shipping to eu-dedicated? Also, can we use temporary top-up from our us-pool while EU is down?

kai: Options and ballpark costs: reflash @ depot — no unit replacement cost, depot labor + 48–72h turnaround (ETA +2–3d). RMA air-exchange — vendor sends replacement units (next-flight) with an RMA return window; expedite fee = $750/unit and customs expedite fee ~€120/unit. If we use pool swap (us -> eu) there are cross-region egress & tax implications and ~24–36h reprovisioning time.

devon: We need 50 GPUs in EU within 2 weeks for a scheduled rollout. Losing 20 units for 3 days is fine if we can top up +30 from other pools. What is allocation for remaining committed units?

andrew-vendor: Current committed allocation for EU for the month: 120 units. After this hold, available immediate stock in EU depots = 38. US pool has ~60 ready units. We can reserve 30 for an inter-region transfer with 36h notice.

maya: Can we do a mixed plan: reflash the 20 at FRA (cheapest), reserve 30 from US pool and route them to EU express (we accept reprovisioning time). That keeps cost down vs air-exchange. Any compliance or customs risk?

andrew-vendor: For inter-region transfer we'll provide commercial invoice and export docs. ETA 36–48h for transit + customs hold variance. If you want a guaranteed 36h door-to-door SLA, choose air-exchange (extra fees apply).

raj: For mitigations on our side: we can delay non-critical rollout nodes and re-balance scheduled jobs to dedicated pools to avoid headroom loss. Also setting temporary routing policy to prefer models with shorter seq lengths to reduce token throughput while capacity is constrained.

ops-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-4123. Linked PR for k8s rollback candidate: https://internal/reviews/987 — add oncall@infra for visibility.

devon: OK — plan approved: 1) reflash 20 at FRA (depot requal) 2) reserve 30 from US pool and request transfer with 36h notice 3) ops to throttle non-critical workloads and monitor SLOs.

kai: Tagging costs: depot reflash ~€0/unit + labor, transfer reserve (30 units) no reservation fee but shipping + customs ~€95/unit expected. If you later want guaranteed air-exchange, conversion fee = $750/unit.

andrew-vendor: I'll schedule depot reflashes starting tomorrow morning and flag 30 US units for hold. ETA for first reflashed units back to EU depot = ~60h. I'll attach the RMA paperwork to the incident if anything changes.

maya: Thanks — devon, raj, please confirm when you've updated routing policies and we can close the loop here. :thumbsup:

devon: will do. Updating canaries now and adding a small eval to detect NIC link flaps post-provision.

raj: added smoke test to provisioning pipeline to detect `mlx5` fw mismatch and auto-fail early.

andrew-vendor: cheers, will update status in INC-2026-4123 and ping when ships are complete.

ops-bot: Reminder: if reflashes fail on >5% units escalate to vendor-svc-lead for RMA air-exchange approval.
